title: Vishram Prasad Chaurasiya v. State of U.P.
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner relegated to a fresh clause 6.5 representation.
headnote: On a writ raising grievances against Purvanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd., the Division Bench held that the appropriate remedy is to approach the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition was disposed of with a direction to file a fresh representation within two weeks; the Executive Engineer must consider all points of objection and pass a reasoned speaking order, preferably within six weeks of receipt.
facts: Vishram Prasad Chaurasiya invoked the writ jurisdiction of the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and officers of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd., Varanasi Division, including the Executive Engineer arrayed as respondent no. 2. Counsel for the Nigam appeared. The petition raised unspecified grievances against the distribution licensee. The Court heard both sides. The order records no connection, meter, or bill particulars and does not decide the underlying supply dispute on merits.

holding_units.topic: representation to Executive Engineer as appropriate remedy
holding_units.holding: For grievances raised in the writ against the Nigam, the appropriate remedy is to approach the Executive Engineer, Purvanchal Vidyut Vitaran Nigam Ltd., Varanasi Division, invoking clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petitioner shall file a fresh representation with a copy of the order within two weeks; on such filing the Executive Engineer is obliged to deal with it strictly in accordance with law, considering all points of objection, and to pass a reasoned speaking order preferably within six weeks of receipt.

principle_tags.application: The Court treated a clause 6.5 representation to the Executive Engineer as the appropriate remedy for the petitioner's grievances against the Nigam and disposed of the writ on that footing.
The writ was not decided on merits; the petitioner was directed to the statutory clause 6.5 machinery instead of a merits grant or refusal in the High Court.
Respondent no. 2 (Executive Engineer, PuVVNL, Varanasi Division) was directed to decide a fresh clause 6.5 representation by a reasoned speaking order after considering all points of objection.

not_decided.point: merits of the petitioner's grievances against the Nigam
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the underlying supply dispute and left it to the Executive Engineer on a fresh clause 6.5 representation.
